page: OVHcloud r3-16 is a memory-optimized server instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.3 GHz. The configuration includes 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs with 1.0 thread per core, backed by 16.0 GB of RAM, which yields a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 50 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks show a mix of capabilities. The AMD EPYC processor delivers strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance in stress-ng and Geekbench is weaker, falling into the middle 50% and bottom 25% respectively, which is expected given the dual-core configuration. Memory bandwidth tests for large uncached blocks, both read and write, score in the average range, though cached small-block reads are weak.

The server exhibits notable performance trade-offs in highly parallelized or I/O-heavy workloads. Static web serving throughput is poor, ranking in the bottom 10%, and database operations under Passmark and Redis SET operations are weak. LLM inference speeds are also limited, with poor prompt processing for 7B models. Consequently, this instance is best suited for memory-sensitive but compute-light workloads, such as small-scale caching layers, lightweight memory-intensive applications, or basic text processing tasks that benefit from dedicated cores.
description: OVHcloud r3-16 is a memory-optimized virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor operating at 2.3 GHz, it provides 2 dedicated physical cores and 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing a high 8.0 GB of RAM per core ratio. Storage is supported by a bundled 50 GB NVMe SSD. Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, though multi-core execution and memory bandwidth for small cached blocks are weaker. Due to low static web serving throughput and weak database operation scores, this instance is not optimal for high-traffic web hosting or heavy database workloads. Instead, it is best suited for memory-intensive, low-concurrency applications, lightweight caching, and basic text processing tasks that require dedicated CPU resources without massive parallel processing needs.
